Module_clanInfluence_mainInstruction: If the policy changes influence for the issuer's clan or clans in the target kingdom, specify onceDelta and dailyDelta separately; both may be 0. The one-time portion settles on the game day following policy adoption, and the daily portion starts on the same day. Centralization usually gives negative values to other clans and positive values to the issuer's clan. Do not output internal module IDs.
Module_clanInfluence_postprocessRule: The output structure must be {"onceDelta": number, "dailyDelta": number}. Values must be finite and may be positive, negative, or 0. onceDelta executes only once on the next game day; dailyDelta executes each day while the policy is active, without reclaiming historical accumulation. If both are 0, omit the effect.
Module_clanInfluence_editableUnderstandi: Clan influence represents political capital, aristocratic power, the degree of centralization, and vassal standing for the issuer's clan or clans in the target kingdom. When a policy directly changes these power relationships, clan influence is an actual consequence. Centralization usually weakens other clans and strengthens the issuer's clan, but must still follow the original policy and its execution path.
Module_clanInfluence_editableEvaluationP: The immediate change settles once on the game day following policy adoption; the ongoing change settles daily starting on that same day while the policy remains active. Ordinary native policies commonly change daily influence by about ±0.2 to ±1, and exceptional monarch-level policies may reach about +3. A custom policy that explicitly changes power structures should not remain at symbolic changes of 0.1 to 0.5 without reason. One-time changes: mild prestige or interest adjustments usually warrant ±10 to ±25 per clan; explicit political rewards, punishments, or transfers of power warrant ±25 to ±60; major centralization, weakening vassals, granting privileges, or widespread noble conflict warrants ±60 to ±120; restructuring governance or handling an existential state crisis may warrant ±120 to ±250. Daily changes: mild continuing effects warrant ±0.5 to ±1; explicit institutional changes warrant ±1 to ±3; major sustained redistribution of power warrants ±3 to ±6; extreme centralization, systematic deprivation, or extraordinary political mobilization warrants ±6 to ±10. Use both components only when the policy causes both an immediate change in political capital on adoption and a subsequent ongoing institution. Do not mechanically double-count the same effect or divide per-clan values because there are many target clans or the policy is long-term or permanent. Low fiscal cost does not mean low influence: judge the depth of power changes, execution authority, noble compliance or resistance, and sustained execution capability.

Module_kingdomStabilityOnce_postprocessR: A one-time stability change when the policy formally takes effect in the target kingdom. Positive values raise stability and negative values lower it; the final changes value must be an integer. Only kingdom or vassal policies may use it; local policies may not. Module_clanLeaderRelationOnce_retrievalT: Personal relations, favor, support, aversion, resentment or gratitude of other clan leaders, lords or vassals toward the policy publisher or issuer. Attitude changes caused by benefits or harm, loss of privileges, recognition of honor, political offenses or oppression; does not change the numerical political influence of a clan. Excludes the issuer's clan and settles relation points once per unique clan leader on the next game day.
Module_clanLeaderRelationOnce_catalogSum: One-time issuer relation change with other clan leaders
Module_clanLeaderRelationOnce_mainInstru: If the policy makes lords in the affected area or target kingdom, excluding the publisher’s clan, more supportive of or hostile toward the publisher, specify a one-time relation change. Positive improves relations, negative worsens them; settle on the next game day after adoption. Player-policy publishers are fixed to the player at publication; ruler-policy publishers are fixed to the ruler who adopted the policy.
Module_clanLeaderRelationOnce_postproces: value must be finite and settles as integer relation points. Deduplicate by clan; settle once per current clan leader. Skip the publisher’s entire clan, eliminated clans and targets without valid leaders. Positive changes retain native diplomacy bonuses and randomized rounding, and relations remain limited to the native -100 to 100 range.
Module_clanLeaderRelationOnce_editableUn: Clan leader relation reflects other lords' support for or resentment toward the publisher in affected areas or target kingdoms. When policies directly benefit, harm, insult, honor or oppress these lords or involve them in conflicts of interest, leader relations are a one-time consequence. Exclude the publisher's entire clan and clans without a valid leader.
Module_clanLeaderRelationOnce_editableEv: Positive improves relations and negative worsens them; judge integer relation points. Changes occur on the game day after adoption. Exclude the publisher's entire clan, and settle once per other current clan leader. Mild courtesies, inconvenience or limited benefits usually warrant ±1 to ±3 per leader; clear benefits, losses, honors or political offense ±4 to ±8; major privileges, heavy losses, public humiliation, strong oppression or significant interest conflicts ±9 to ±15; lifesaving gratitude, severe betrayal, systematic persecution or events capable of changing political alignment ±16 to ±30. Do not dilute each leader's change to 1 point because many clans are targeted or the effect settles only once. Do not use high values merely for ornate wording. Intensity follows each leader's actual benefits, losses, honor, oppression and political risks; native relation limits still apply.
Module_constructionPerDay_retrievalText: Construction power, engineering, buildings, infrastructure, construction work, artisans, fortifications and public works; fixed daily construction-point changes per target town or castle.
Module_constructionPerDay_catalogSummary: Daily construction point change for towns or castles
Module_constructionPerDay_mainInstructio: If the policy continuously changes target towns’ or castles’ daily construction power, engineering capacity or construction investment, explain targets, direction, intensity and reasons in numericIntent; do not output module IDs or numbers.
Module_constructionPerDay_postprocessRul: payload contains only one finite numeric value. It is the fixed construction points directly added to native building projects daily per target town or castle: positive speeds construction, negative slows it. It is not a percentage.
Module_constructionPerDay_editableUnders: Building construction power is affected only by explicit building construction or repairs, artisans, labor, building materials, engineering transport, construction organization, stoppages or damage to works. Development, prosperity, subsidies, tax exemptions, tax increases, general fiscal spending and reasonable elaboration of execution methods must not independently be interpreted as construction measures.
Module_constructionPerDay_editableEvalua: Judge fixed construction power added or removed directly per affected town or castle daily, without percentage conversion. Small-scale changes: ±20 to ±60; sustained expansion of construction resources: +60 to +150; major nationwide construction: +300 to +1000. Extreme mobilization, huge dedicated investment or a player's explicit demand for extreme intensity may reach 2 to 4 times this range, including more than +1000, only when execution paths and resource commitments are sufficiently clear. Use proportionate negatives only if the policy directly obstructs construction, causes labor loss or material shortages, or damages the construction system.
Module_foodPerDay_retrievalText: Town food, granaries, food stocks, supply, famine, relief, rationing, grain requisitions and transport supplies; daily food changes per target town.
Module_foodPerDay_mainInstruction: If the policy continuously changes target towns’ food stocks or daily supplies, explain the targets, direction, intensity and reasons in numericIntent; do not output module IDs or numbers.
Module_foodPerDay_postprocessRule: payload contains only one finite numeric value. It is the fixed food-stock points settled daily per target town: positive adds food, negative removes it. Do not convert it into a cumulative value for the entire policy.
Module_foodPerDay_editableUnderstandingP: Food stocks are mainly affected by production, procurement, storage, transport, requisition, relief, army-ration consumption, blockades and destruction. When policies continuously change town food supplies through these mechanisms, food is a direct consequence. Procurement, subsidies and economic development do not themselves imply stock depletion. Only direct requisition, consumption or destruction of local stocks produces negative changes.
Module_foodPerDay_editableEvaluationProm: Judge daily stock changes per affected town. Mild impact: ±1 to ±3; regular food policies, transport, requisition or storage adjustments: ±3 to ±8; large-scale relief, forced requisitions or army-ration allocation: ±8 to ±15; major nationwide supplies, famine, blockades or comprehensive grain requisition: ±18 to ±30; extreme disasters or nationwide food operations: ±30 to ±45.
Module_hearthPerDay_retrievalText: Village hearths, population, rural development, migrant resettlement, land reclamation, population loss and village prosperity; daily hearth changes in villages attached to lawful parent targets.
Module_hearthPerDay_mainInstruction: If the policy continuously changes hearths, rural population or land reclamation in villages attached to target towns or castles, explain the target scope, direction, intensity and reasons naturally in numericIntent. Villages have no independent targets; do not output module IDs or numbers.
Module_hearthPerDay_postprocessRule: payload contains only one finite numeric value. Lawful parent targets deterministically expand into their attached villages; the value is fixed daily hearth points per village, positive for increases and negative for decreases. Villages do not accept independent target handles.
Module_hearthPerDay_editableUnderstandin: Village hearths represent population and labor. They are mainly affected by labor availability, safety, corvée, resettlement, migration, flight, land reclamation, slaughter and disasters. When policies continuously change population in villages attached to the relevant towns or castles through these mechanisms, hearths are a direct consequence.
Module_hearthPerDay_editableEvaluationPr: Judge daily changes per affected village. Mild impact: ±0.1 to ±0.5; regular corvée, resettlement, labor recovery or migration: ±0.5 to ±1.5; strong immigration, wartime flight, oppressive taxes or large-scale forced labor: ±2 to ±4; nationwide population support, slaughter, disasters or forced migration: ±4 to ±7; extreme population changes or catastrophes: ±7 to ±10.
Module_kingdomStability_retrievalText: Kingdom stability, political stability, central authority, national unrest, rebellion risk, institutional shocks and political crises; settles once on the game day following policy adoption.
Module_kingdomStability_catalogSummary: One-time kingdom stability change on the next game day
Module_kingdomStability_mainInstruction: If the policy directly changes kingdom-level political stability, central authority or unrest risk, specify a one-time stability change. It settles on the next game day after adoption, does not stack by town count, and is unavailable to local policies.
Module_kingdomStability_postprocessRule: payload contains only one finite numeric value, settled once as integer stability points on the next game day: positive raises stability, negative lowers it. It does not repeat with duration or stack by town count, and is prohibited in local scope.
Module_kingdomStability_editableUndersta: Kingdom stability means national political structure and governing order. It is mainly affected by public confidence, fiscal prestige, vassal trust, royal legitimacy, war victories and defeats, noble interests, domestic fragmentation risk and decisive victories. Pure administrative or ordinary local numeric changes are usually not kingdom stability consequences; positive or negative direction requires direct political causality.
Module_kingdomStability_editableEvaluati: Positive means improved stability; negative means greater unrest. Judge integer stability points. Clear changes to public confidence, fiscal prestige, vassal trust, royal legitimacy or fragmentation risk: ±4 to ±7; major reforms, nationwide mobilization, broad noble conflicts or severe political crises: ±7 to ±14; the verge of civil war, national survival, collapse of governance or decisive victory: ±14 to ±22. Settle only once on the game day after policy adoption; do not stack by town count.
Module_kingdomVillageRaidBan_retrievalTe: The policy prohibits lords and lord parties of the issuer’s own kingdom from proactively raiding any village. The target is fixed automatically to the issuer’s kingdom; it does not protect its villages from foreign raids or affect other kingdoms.
Module_kingdomVillageRaidBan_catalogSumm: Ban proactive village raids by the issuing kingdom's lords
Module_kingdomVillageRaidBan_mainInstruc: Select this effect only if the policy explicitly prohibits, stops or restricts lords of the issuer’s kingdom from burning, attacking or raiding villages. There is no selectable target kingdom: selection affects only the issuer’s kingdom. It does not protect domestic villages from foreign lords or constrain any other kingdom. Do not output module IDs.
Module_kingdomVillageRaidBan_postprocess: payload must be exactly {}. Presence means that lord parties of the issuer’s kingdom are prohibited from proactively raiding any Village; there is no number, level or stacked intensity. targetHandles may only copy the sole issuer-kingdom handle provided for this module by the execution directory.
Module_kingdomVillageRaidBan_editableUnd: A kingdom village raid ban is a national rule from the publisher prohibiting its own kingdom's lords and lord parties from proactively burning, attacking or raiding any village. The target is automatically fixed to the publisher's kingdom; foreign kingdoms cannot be selected. It is not a global shield protecting the publisher's villages and does not prevent foreign lords from burning villages.
Module_kingdomVillageRaidBan_editableEva: Judge only whether the policy explicitly establishes a continuing rule against village raids by lords of the publisher's own kingdom. When matched, activate the complete prohibition without intensity or probability assessment. Multiple active policies still produce only one prohibition. General care for the population, improved security, protected agriculture, punishment of enemies or defense of certain villages does not qualify without prohibiting one's own lords from burning villages.
Module_loyaltyPerDay_retrievalText: Town loyalty, popular support, identification, oppression, autonomy, cultural conflict, rebellion tendencies and pacifying the population; daily loyalty changes per target town.
Module_loyaltyPerDay_mainInstruction: If the policy continuously changes target towns’ popular loyalty, political identification or resistance, explain the targets, direction, intensity and reasons in numericIntent; do not output module IDs or numbers.
Module_loyaltyPerDay_postprocessRule: payload contains only one finite numeric value. It is the fixed loyalty points settled daily per target town: positive raises loyalty, negative lowers it. Do not calculate the entire policy period first and then distribute it across days.
Module_loyaltyPerDay_editableUnderstandi: Loyalty is mainly affected by perceived fairness, cultural identification, autonomy, oppression, fear, honor and the distribution of interests. When policies directly and continuously affect towns' popular support, political identification or resistance, loyalty is a direct consequence. Economic prosperity alone cannot substitute for political identification.
Module_loyaltyPerDay_editableEvaluationP: Judge actual daily changes per affected town; do not first calculate the entire duration and divide by days. Mild impact: ±0.1 to ±0.4; regular reassurance, tax burdens, fairness, cultural treatment or autonomy adjustments: ±0.4 to ±1.2; major reforms, strong oppression, heavy-tax relief, broad relief programs, honorary privileges or clear discrimination: ±2 to ±6; extreme tyranny, major rescue of the population, severe betrayal, systematic persecution or near-rebellion stimuli: ±4 to ±12.
Module_militiaPerDay_retrievalText: Militia, local armed forces, defense, conscription, local militia training, disbanding militia and settlement defense; daily militia changes per target settlement.
Module_militiaPerDay_mainInstruction: If the policy continuously changes target settlements’ militia recruitment, training or disbanding speed, explain the targets, direction, intensity and reasons in numericIntent; do not output module IDs or numbers.
Module_militiaPerDay_postprocessRule: payload contains only one finite numeric value. It is the fixed militia headcount points settled daily per target settlement: positive adds militia, negative removes it.
Module_militiaPerDay_editableUnderstandi: Militia is mainly affected by training, levies, disbanding, local defense, morale, food and pay, and population pressures. When policies continuously change actual settlement defense headcounts through these mechanisms, militia is a direct consequence. Increasing militia incurs corresponding costs only when the policy actually requisitions food or labor or forces military service.
Module_militiaPerDay_editableEvaluationP: Judge daily changes per affected settlement. Mild impact: ±0.5 to ±1.5; regular training, levies or morale changes: ±1.5 to ±4; strong militia mobilization or local-defense reforms: ±4 to ±8; nationwide war mobilization, large-scale militarization or militia collapse: ±8 to ±12. More than ±12 is reserved for brief extreme war mobilization or severe military collapse.
Module_prosperityPerDay_retrievalText: Town prosperity, commercial development, population and wealth growth, economic depression, investment, market revitalization and long-term development; daily prosperity changes per target town.
Module_prosperityPerDay_mainInstruction: If the policy continuously changes target towns’ prosperity, commercial vitality or overall economic development, explain the targets, direction, intensity and reasons in numericIntent; do not output module IDs or numbers.
Module_prosperityPerDay_postprocessRule: payload contains only one finite numeric value. It is the fixed prosperity points settled daily per target town: positive increases and negative decreases prosperity. Do not convert it into a cumulative policy value or percentage.
Module_prosperityPerDay_editableUndersta: Prosperity is mainly affected by trade, tax burdens, industry and commerce, market confidence, development investment and war damage. When policies continuously change the scale of towns' economies through these mechanisms, prosperity is a direct consequence.
Module_prosperityPerDay_editableEvaluati: Judge daily changes per affected town. Mild impact: ±0.5 to ±2; regular policies: ±2 to ±5; clear economic policies, trade stimulus, damage from tax burdens or war damage: ±5 to ±10; major nationwide investment or disasters: ±12 to ±24; extreme prosperity projects, severe plunder, blockades, famine or national economic catastrophes: ±24 to ±36.
Module_securityPerDay_retrievalText: Town security, crime, patrols, bandits, law enforcement, order, corruption and public safety; daily security changes per target town.
Module_securityPerDay_mainInstruction: If the policy continuously changes target towns’ security, crime control or public order, explain the targets, direction, intensity and reasons in numericIntent; do not output module IDs or numbers.
Module_securityPerDay_postprocessRule: payload contains only one finite numeric value. It is the fixed security points settled daily per target town: positive improves security, negative worsens it.
Module_securityPerDay_editableUnderstand: Security is mainly affected by banditry, patrols, law enforcement, justice, corruption, military rule, suppression and local order. When policies continuously change local safety through these mechanisms, security is a direct consequence.
Module_securityPerDay_editableEvaluation: Judge daily changes per affected town. Mild impact: ±0.1 to ±0.3; regular patrols, law enforcement, anti-corruption or banditry changes: ±0.3 to ±0.7; strong security campaigns, military rule, border disorder or banditry outbreaks: ±0.8 to ±1.5; severe disorder or high-pressure suppression: ±1.5 to ±2.5. More than ±2.5 is reserved for brief extreme internal unrest, bloody suppression or large-scale banditry.
Module_taxIncomePct_retrievalText: Fief, town or castle taxation, tax rates, tax reductions, exemptions, fiscal tax revenue, fief tax income, collection and tax transfers; percentage-point changes to main tax income received by clans owning target towns or castles. General personal or lord income without fiefs or taxation is excluded.
Module_taxIncomePct_catalogSummary: Tax percentage change for clans owning towns or castles
Module_taxIncomePct_mainInstruction: Only if the policy explicitly changes fiefs, towns, castles or taxation and directly affects main tax income of the clans owning target towns or castles, explain burden bearers, beneficiaries, direction, intensity and reasons in numericIntent. General income increases for lords, rulers or other professions without fiefs, towns, castles or taxation do not qualify. Do not output module IDs or numbers.
Module_taxIncomePct_postprocessRule: payload contains only one finite numeric value. It is the percentage-point change in the native main tax income finally received by clans owning target towns or castles: positive increases revenue, negative reduces it. It is not the local population’s tax rate and excludes independent village income and tariffs.
Module_taxIncomePct_editableUnderstandin: Main town and castle tax income means changes in native main tax revenue finally received by clans owning the target fiefs, not amounts extracted from the local population. Use only when the body explicitly involves fiefs, towns, castles or taxation. Raising owner-retained tax rates, collection efficiency or receipts remitted from other regions increases income; tax reductions, exemptions or withholding, transferring or remitting taxes to another party reduces income. General increases in lords', rulers' or other professions' incomes without fiefs or taxation do not qualify. When taxes transfer between parties, represent both the payer and beneficiary separately. Independent village income, tariffs and mere prosperity changes are excluded.
Module_taxIncomePct_editableEvaluationPr: Judge percentage-point changes relative to final native main tax income: positive increases revenue and negative reduces it. Regular tax adjustments: ±5% to ±15%; clear adjustments: ±15% to ±35%; major nationwide taxation: ±20% to ±60%. Changes only to specific groups, industries, regions, periods, tax types or portions of revenue require a proportionate value based on actual coverage. Approach -100% only when all main town and castle taxation in the affected scope is explicitly abolished.
Module_villageProductionPct_retrievalTex: The policy directly raises or lowers all native goods output of administratively attached villages of target towns and castles, including village-type products, horses and other livestock, and common grain, cheese and butter batches. It does not change town food stocks, workshop speed or construction power. Goods circulate through native village inventory, villager transport and TradeBound markets.
Module_villageProductionPct_catalogSumma: Relative native goods output of attached villages
Module_villageProductionPct_mainInstruct: Only when the policy directly changes agriculture, livestock, horse breeding, raw materials or grain-goods output in administratively attached villages of target towns or castles, specify a percentage change relative to native village goods output. It affects village-type products including horses and other livestock and common native grain, cheese and butter batches. It does not directly add town food stocks or change workshop speed or construction power. Goods follow native TradeBound logistics; villages have no independent target handles. Do not output module IDs.
Module_villageProductionPct_postprocessR: payload must be exactly {"value": number}; value must be finite and expresses percentage change relative to final native village goods output. +20 multiplies output by 120%, +100 by 200%; -100 or lower stacked totals set output to zero. It is not a fixed daily item increase. Sum active-policy percentages before scaling both village-type products and common food batches. Lawful parent targets deterministically expand into administratively attached villages; no goods are added directly to any town inventory.
Module_villageProductionPct_editableUnde: Village goods output means all actual goods generated by the native production model in administratively attached villages, including village-type products, horses and other livestock, and common grain, cheese and butter batches. Select only if the policy directly changes agriculture, animal husbandry, breeding, gathering, raw-material processing or food-goods output. Do not mistake town food stocks, workshop production speed, construction power or mere trade circulation for village output. Only the production model changes; goods first enter village inventories and circulate through native villager transport and TradeBound markets.
Module_villageProductionPct_editableEval: The value is a percentage change relative to the final current native village goods output, not a fixed item count. Native base daily village output is low and actual inventory additions use randomized rounding, so positive policies need perceptible intensity. Do not assess clearly effective policies at only +5% to +15%. +20 multiplies output by 1.2, +50 by 1.5, +100 by 2, and -100 sets it to zero. Mild tools, road maintenance or seasonal support usually use +20% to +40%, or -10% to -20% for negatives. Explicit agricultural, husbandry or breeding institutions use about +40% to +80%, or -20% to -40%. Large irrigation, land reform or strong production reforms use about +80% to +150%; forced requisition, severe labor loss or disasters use -40% to -70%. Extreme positive policies changing regional economic structure may reach +150% to +250%; devastating disasters or total plunder use -70% to -100%. Add policies first; the multiplier minimum is 0 and there is no extra positive hard cap, but negative assessments must not be below -100%.
Module_volunteerProductionGrowthPct_retr: The policy directly raises or lowers replenishment and growth speed of unrecruited volunteers in target fiefs. The same relative percentage scales empty-slot replenishment checks and the frequency at which existing volunteers enter native upgrade attempts. This is an abstract policy result, requires no recruitment station or training camp, and does not directly recruit, grant troop experience or guarantee upgrades.
Module_volunteerProductionGrowthPct_cata: Relative volunteer refill and growth-attempt frequency
Module_volunteerProductionGrowthPct_main: Only when the policy directly changes replenishment of unrecruited volunteers, recovery of recruitable slots or volunteer growth in target fiefs, specify a change relative to native daily check frequency. Empty and occupied slots use the same value: empty slots affect replenishment checks; occupied slots affect only entry into native upgrade attempts and retain subsequent native upgrade checks. It is not recruitment-pool refreshing, requires no station or camp, does not directly add party members or grant experience to lord parties or garrisons. General army expansion, training or better active troops without changing volunteers does not qualify. Do not output module IDs.
Module_volunteerProductionGrowthPct_post: payload must be exactly {"value": number}; value must be finite and expresses percentage change relative to native daily check frequency. +20 multiplies native probability by 120%, +100 by 200%; -100 or lower stacked totals set probability to zero. These are not absolute probability points. Sum percentages from active policies, scale using native formulas, and clamp final probability to 0 to 1. Empty-slot replenishment and existing-volunteer entry into native upgrade attempts share one value.
Module_volunteerProductionGrowthPct_edit: Volunteer replenishment and growth directly changes unrecruited notable volunteer slots in target fiefs. One value affects two states: empty slots change native volunteer-replenishment checks; occupied slots change the frequency of entering native upgrade attempts. The latter still requires subsequent native upgrade checks, so upgrades are not guaranteed. This is an abstract policy result: recruitment stations, training camps or other fixed facilities need not be specified, and it must not be described as recruitment-pool refreshing. It does not directly recruit soldiers, grant hero skills, grant troop experience to ordinary soldiers in lord parties or garrisons, or affect militia.

The value is a percentage change relative to native daily check frequency, not absolute probability points. +20 multiplies native probability by 1.2, +50 by 1.5, +100 by 2, and -100 sets it to zero. Mild improvements or impediments usually use ±10% to ±25%; explicit institutional changes about ±25% to ±60%; strong reforms about ±60% to ±100%. More than +100% requires very strong policy evidence, but runtime follows the old policy system without an extra positive hard cap. Add policies first; the multiplier minimum is 0, and final probability is limited to 0 to 1. Use soldier elite training alongside this only if the policy separately grants experience to ordinary soldiers already in lord parties or garrisons.
Module_heroGold_retrievalText: Personal income and denar balances of the player, policy publisher, rulers, lords, clan leaders, notables or native professions through army pay, salaries, trade, industry, subsidies, rewards, punishments or confiscations. Local army pay, salaries, allowances or fiscal subsidies with no other personal recipient mean positive denars for current owner-clan leaders of affected settlements. May specify a one-time change on the next game day and subsequent daily changes. Startup, upkeep, construction investment and administrative budgets are excluded.
Module_heroGold_catalogSummary: Personal denar changes for characters and native professions
Module_heroGold_mainInstruction: When policy measures reasonably and directly change personal economic gains through army pay, salaries, trade, industry, subsidies, rewards, punishments or confiscations, the model judges affected identities, direction and intensity without requiring professions or exact denar amounts verbatim. Local army pay, salaries, allowances or fiscal subsidies with no other personal recipient default to positive denars for current owner-clan leaders of affected settlements; retain settlement binding and select settlement handles, never nationwide lord or soldier character sets. Use character targets only when the body directly names individuals or professions. Continuing income, stipends, salaries, allowances and regular subsidies default to dailyDelta with onceDelta 0; explicit single rewards, bonuses, arrears, fines and confiscations default to onceDelta with dailyDelta 0. Fill both only when both are explicit. Settle per final character; values may be positive, negative or 0. A lord owning multiple affected settlements settles only once.
